retrieval: Project Gutenberg supplied-edition witness mirrored by GITenberg, transcoded to UTF-8 without changing text or line endings; hash identifies retained UTF-8 witness.
scope: Whole original-English lyrics and short standalone poems; translations, fragments and extended narrative or sequence units excluded individually; no artificial splitting.
deduplication: Parent batch integration compares eligible units against the existing corpus and this batch.
extraction: Explicit source-line boundary ledger; verse-only extraction removes title/subtitle/section headings, epigraphs, publishing and editorial apparatus. Long-line continuations joined only by listed source-line groups in Easter Eve, Te Deum, and The Bather; all original words and punctuation retained.
notes: Front-matter prose, tables of contents, headings, ornaments and isolated prefatory epigraphs are apparatus, not candidate poems.
All supplied editions checked directly on canonical Project Gutenberg pages; mirror retrieval preserves accented original spelling.

Joint book attribution retained because the supplied edition does not individually sign the poems. Hunting-Song is separately anthologized as a complete song, not extracted here from a play. Verlaine and Nocturne: In Anjou are English poems about poets, not translations.
